Business data map: Bunkai TMS

Generated 2026-11-13 from the staging database (read-only inspector role), upex-bunkai-tms migrations at origin/staging 63d5e7e3 and the staging OpenAPI spec. Seeded from the legacy .context/business/business-data-map.md. Columns are not listed: query the database for schema detail.

Executive summary

Bunkai is a test-management system built around one promise: every test traces back to a User Story and forward to its execution evidence. Its data is organised as a tenant tree. A Workspace (the paying tenant) holds Projects; each Project has a tree of Modules holding User Stories and their Acceptance Criteria, usually imported from the team's own Jira.

QA engineers and AI agents author ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases) that must anchor to a story and at least one criterion, assemble them into Tests, and execute Tests as Runs. A Run copies the Test's chain at start, so later ATC edits never rewrite history. A failed Run step becomes a Bug carrying its full context. Around that chain sit planning (Test Plans, Milestones), collaboration (chat, notifications, activity log), access (members, invites, personal access tokens) and the business layer (plans, Stripe billing, grace periods, workspace deletion and export).

Actors: workspace owners, admins, members and viewers (people), plus machine callers (CLI, AI agents, CI) through tokens. Every table is workspace-scoped and protected by Row Level Security; multi-table writes go through SECURITY DEFINER functions so they land or roll back as a whole.

Key relationships

  • Deleting a workspace cascades to every workspace-scoped table, but a workspace is only soft-deleted first; the physical delete happens at purge time.
  • An ATC anchors to exactly one User Story (RESTRICT: a story with ATCs cannot be hard-deleted) and to criteria through the N:M link.
  • test_steps reference ATCs with RESTRICT: an ATC used by a Test cannot be hard-deleted, only archived.
  • A Run references its Test and environment with RESTRICT; its snapshot rows reference ATCs and ATC steps with SET NULL, so history survives even if the source disappears.
  • A Bug's run, step and ATC links are SET NULL; its project and module links cascade.
  • Secrets live in sibling *_secrets tables (tokens, invites, magic links) readable only by the service role.

Entity pattern: secrets split from their records

Tokens, invites and magic links each keep two tables: the visible record (who, when, scopes, status) and a *_secrets sibling holding only the hash (and, for magic links, a hashed client IP). The secrets tables are readable only by service_role. The QA inspector roles can read access_tokens and still never see a hash.

Jira API tokens go one step further: they are not in any table but in Supabase Vault, read only by a service-role function after the caller is authorised. Deleting a Jira connection purges its Vault secret through a trigger.

Entity: ATC (archive, version, execution status)

  • Archive, not delete: ATCs carry archive columns guarded by a trigger (atcs_guard_archive_columns), and can be restored.
  • Version: every edit bumps version; the API edit path requires it as an optimistic lock.
  • Execution status (pass · fail · blocked · skipped · running · unrun) reflects executions; it is set by Runs and is not editable by authors.
  • Search: a trigger refreshes the full-text vector on every insert and update.
  • Enumerations: layer UI/API/Unit; priority Critical/High/Medium/Low; technique Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise.

Entity: Workspace (plan, effective plan, soft delete)

  • Stored plan vs effective plan: workspaces.plan is never rewritten when a renewal fails. bunkai_effective_plan evaluates a cloud workspace as community once its 14-day grace window has ended; limits read the effective plan.
  • Project limit: a BEFORE INSERT trigger on projects refuses the insert (project_limit_reached) at 3 projects on community, 50 on cloud; enterprise is unlimited.
  • Soft delete: deletion sets the soft-delete columns, revokes tokens and pending invites, and cuts access for everyone, owner included. A workspace_deletions row (no FK) records the request and the purge deadline.
  • General chat channel: created by a trigger on workspace insert.

Entity: Run snapshot

Starting a Run copies the Test's ATCs into run_atcs and their steps into run_steps, with denormalised titles. Results are recorded on these copies. A later ATC edit, archive or even deletion does not change what a past Run shows: the links back to the source ATC and step become NULL instead of cascading. A trigger stamps the source ATC id on each run_atcs row.

Flow: sign-up and first workspace

  1. The visitor signs up; a mandatory six-digit OTP confirms the account (or magic link / OAuth).
  2. POST /api/v1/workspaces runs bunkai_bootstrap_workspace: workspace plus owner membership in one transaction.
  3. A trigger creates the workspace's general chat channel.

Rules: one owner per workspace; the creator becomes owner. Sequence: business-api-context section journey-onboarding.

Flow: invites, membership and tokens

  1. An owner or admin creates an invite (role viewer, member or admin); the token hash goes to workspace_invite_secrets and the link is returned, not emailed.
  2. The invitee accepts with a matching email: membership upsert and acceptance stamp in one transaction.
  3. Tokens are minted from a session; the hash goes to access_token_secrets. Revocation sets revoked_at.
  4. Deleting the workspace revokes all its tokens and pending invites in the same transaction.

Sequences: business-api-context sections journey-invite and journey-pat-lifecycle.

Flow: Jira connection and import

  1. An owner or admin saves the workspace Jira connection; the token goes to Vault.
  2. A member enqueues an import: an import_jobs row in queued; at most one active import per project.
  3. After the 202 response a background task pages Jira, converts descriptions from Atlassian Document Format, extracts acceptance criteria and upserts stories and criteria.
  4. The job ends completed or failed; per-issue errors are recorded on the job.

Rule: no connection means the import is refused (409 jira_not_connected). Sequence: journey-jira-import in the API map.

Flow: ATC authoring

  1. Create: bunkai_create_atc writes the ATC, steps, assertions and criterion links together.
  2. Edit: bunkai_update_atc with the expected version (API) or last-write-wins (browser).
  3. Bulk edit: one field on up to 200 ATCs, each processed on its own.
  4. Archive and restore keep the row; an ATC used by a Test cannot be hard-deleted.

Rule: at least one User Story and one acceptance criterion per ATC. Sequence: journey-atc-authoring in the API map.

Flow: story readiness

  1. A story moves to ready_to_test through bunkai_set_user_story_status, which locks the story and re-counts its active criteria.
  2. The move is refused while the story has zero active criteria.
  3. Archiving the last active criterion drops the story back to draft in the same transaction.

See state-user-story.

Flow: test assembly

  1. A Test is created and ATCs are added as ordered test_steps; steps can be reordered and tagged.
  2. automation_status tracks whether the Test is manual-only, a candidate or automated.

Rule: a Run needs at least one executable step in the Test.

Flow: run execution and evidence

  1. Start: bunkai_create_run snapshots the chain, validates the environment and opens the Run as running; a 24h same-token window de-duplicates retries.
  2. Steps are marked in any order; image evidence is uploaded to Storage as pending and becomes visible on commit.
  3. Finish closes the Run passed or failed; abort closes it aborted with a 3-500 character reason. Untouched steps become skipped.
  4. Agents may submit a finished Run in one call; run_submission_keys make retries return the same Run.
  5. Silent runs are closed by the sweeps (see automatic-processes).

Activity rows run.started / run.finished feed notifications. Sequence: journey-run-execution in the API map.

Flow: bug filing and lifecycle

  1. Run-linked: only run_step_id is sent; project, module, run and ATC are derived, and the step must be failed.
  2. Standalone: project and module are sent directly.
  3. bugs_check_consistency (BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE) refuses inconsistent links.
  4. Status moves one stage forward per call; assignment changes emit their own activity events.

See state-bug.

Flow: test plans and milestones

  1. A Test Plan groups Tests of a project; Milestones are dated targets (today to 5 years ahead, unique name per project).
  2. Plans link to milestones through milestone_plans.
  3. Closing a plan (creator, admin or owner) writes verdict, summary, closer, time and a frozen progress snapshot together; reopening clears them and keeps both events in history.

See state-test-plan.

Flow: plan upgrade, renewals and dunning

  1. The owner opens a checkout session (row written before Stripe is called; one open session per workspace).
  2. The signed webhook applies cloud only when the session is paid; expired or failed sessions release the lock. Event ids are stored for dedupe.
  3. A failed renewal sets payment_failed and opens a 14-day grace window from the first failure; the owner can retry (retry_pending).
  4. A paid invoice moves the state to recovered and ends the window. If the window ends unpaid, the workspace is evaluated as community.

See state-checkout-session and state-payment.

Flow: data export, deletion, restore and purge

  1. Export (owner, browser session only): a workspace_exports job processed in the background; one active export per workspace.
  2. Delete (owner, browser session only): soft delete, tokens and invites revoked, access cut for everyone, deletion record with a 30-day purge deadline; a notice email is sent.
  3. Restore during the 30 days brings the workspace back.
  4. A nightly pg_cron job purges workspaces past their deadline; the deletion record survives the purge.

See state-workspace.

Flow: notifications and daily digest

  1. Activity rows for run and bug events fire triggers that create in-app notifications.
  2. Chat @mentions notify each mentioned active member once.
  3. Every day at 08:00 UTC a cron route claims one digest slot per user and emails unread notifications through Resend; a failed send leaves them unread for the next day.

Preferences choose channel (in-app, email) per family: run lifecycle, bug lifecycle, mentions.

Integration: Jira Cloud

AspectDetail
Data flowInbound: stories and acceptance criteria (import). Outbound: connection checks only.
Dependent flowsStory import; ATC anchoring depends on imported stories.
Failure behaviourImport job fails or records per-issue errors; existing data untouched. Bug sync to Jira is configured per project but nothing sends bugs yet.

Integration: Stripe

AspectDetail
Data flowOutbound: checkout sessions, payment method, invoices, retries. Inbound: signed webhooks that change plan and payment state.
Dependent flowsPlan upgrade, renewals, dunning, invoices.
Failure behaviourCheckout answers 502/503; a missed webhook leaves the plan unchanged until Stripe redelivers (unknown sessions answer 5xx on purpose).

Integration: Resend (email)

AspectDetail
Data flowOutbound only: daily digest and workspace deletion notice.
Dependent flowsNotifications digest, workspace deletion.
Failure behaviourA failed digest marks the slot failed and leaves notifications unread for the next day. Invites are never emailed.

Integration: Supabase platform

AspectDetail
Data flowAuth (identities, OTP, OAuth), Postgres with RLS, Vault (Jira tokens), Storage (evidence images), pg_cron (sweeps and purge).
Dependent flowsEverything.
Failure behaviourAuth outage blocks sign-in; Storage outage blocks evidence upload (503) but not step marking.

Discovery gaps

  • pg_cron state not readable: the read-only role has no access to schema cron; job names and schedules come from migrations, not from the live cron.job table.
  • Legacy correction: the legacy map's bunkai_ready_to_test_gate RPC does not exist on staging; the gate is bunkai_set_user_story_status. The legacy also stated there was no cron; there are four pg_cron jobs and two Vercel crons.
  • Bug sync sender: project_tracker_settings and the bug sync_state columns exist, but no application code sends bugs to Jira.
  • feature_flags: still in the schema; the legacy map found it never queried. Not re-verified in this pass.
  • Export storage: where export files are stored and how long they live was not traced.
  • Membership transitions: suspension and removal rules were only partially traced (removal has its own RPC and failpoints).
  • Row counts: staging holds heavy automated test data; table sizes do not reflect real usage and are deliberately left out.
